rationale: #1188 incident spelling. Real Bash folds the backslash-escaped space into ONE argument --time-style=+%m-%d %H:%M and keeps docs/evidence a separate argument; the measured unquoted `a\ b` row of docs/evidence/1188-backslash-whitespace-investigation.md gives one argument `a b` (bash -c argv oracle: [a b]). Nothing here is a word-boundary or operator disagreement.

#1188 incident spelling, continuation between options. Real Bash ends `--json number,title` at the escaped LF and passes `-q` and `.title` as two further arguments; the measured separator-continuation row of the same evidence document gives two arguments `a` and `b` (NUL-delimited argv oracle: [a, b]). A word already closed before the backslash, so the join crosses no word.
Same shape as the escaped-space incident row, reduced to one argument. Real Bash prints <a b>: the escaped space stays inside a single lexical word and yields one argument.

Same shape as the separator-continuation incident row, reduced to two arguments. Real Bash prints <a> then <b>: the trailing space closed the first word, so the escaped LF separates words instead of joining them.

Real Bash prints <ab>, ONE argument: backslash immediately followed by LF joins two parts of the same lexical word (measured mid-word row; NUL-delimited argv oracle: [ab]). The facade models two words `a` and `b` for this input (evidence table, mid-word row), so admitting it would trust a wrong word boundary. Denied on purpose.

Bash does not treat backslash+TAB as a line continuation: the backslash stays literal and real Bash prints one argument carrying the backslash and the TAB (measured unquoted backslash+TAB row, output <a\tb>). The facade models two words (evidence table), so the word split is a real disagreement. Denied on purpose.
